R1.method: normal-mixture (Hoeffding-type sub-Gaussian) CS, V_n = n, rho = 100, two-sided alpha = 0.05; NO running intersection (the target moves with n)
R1.gate_status: not established: lower bound -0.1320 <= -0.03 at n = 295
R1.target: running conditional mean (1/n) sum_{k<=n} mu_k, mu_k = E[Z_k | F_(k-1)], F_k = sigma(design information independent of future outcomes, revealed pair data up to k)
R1.filtration: F_k = sigma(design information independent of future outcomes, revealed pair data up to k)
R1.assumption: bounded scores and the stated filtration only (Z_k - mu_k is a martingale difference with range 2); no iid / stationarity / independence-of-pairs assumption
R1.interpretation_condition: the reading mu_k = [m(s_k,t_k)+m(t_k,s_k)]/2 and E_design[mu_bar] = theta_N hold ONLY under an additional orientation-independent, history-independent stable episode-law model (thermal state, order and caching can affect latency); not assumed for the CS
R1.joint_coverage_note: the separate 95% CSs for NB and for the success difference are NOT a joint 95% region
R1.post_hoc_note: rho = 100 was fixed after the outcomes of this experiment had been seen (post hoc); fixing it before computing these intervals does not preregister the analysis

R2.method: corrected hedged betting CS (src/wincs.py, (K+ + K-)/2 vs 1/delta), decided-pair win-ratio CS, preregistered one-sided e-processes
R2.model: unconditional MODEL-BASED inference over hypothetical iid rosters with independent stable episode laws; F = past revealed pair data plus design information independent of future task values (NOT the entire realized roster); not a guarantee conditional on the curated benchmark
R2.filtration: F = past revealed pair data plus design information independent of future task values (NOT the entire realized roster)

monitor.status_R1: DESCRIPTIVE. The fixed-stake one-sided e-processes test the pointwise conditional null (harm: mu_k >= 0 for every k); no guarantee about the running conditional mean or theta_N is claimed from a crossing, and no new theorem is imported.
monitor.status_R2: Under the R2 model E[Z_k | F_(k-1)] = theta_P for the stated (coarse) filtration, so the crossings carry the anytime type-I guarantee at alpha for theta_P; model-based, not conditional on the curated roster.

e2.target: assignment-averaged same-task preference over the roster: (1/591) sum_t E[S_t], the expectation taken over the orientation coins (which fix the pass in which each workflow sees task t) and over episode randomness; S_t = h(Y_B(t), Y_A(t)) from the one A and one B episode of task t
e2.clusters: 295 design pairs of design.json (shared AB/BA coin, complementary pass positions) + singleton unpaired task mbpp/256; G = 296
e2.counterexample: Two tasks forming one design pair; both workflows are identical within a task and period. Task 1 succeeds in pass 1 and fails in pass 2; task 2 fails in pass 1 and succeeds in pass 2. Under one fair AB/BA orientation the two same-task success scores are (1, 1); under the other they are (-1, -1). Each task's mean score is 0, but Var((S1+S2)/2) = 1 while s^2/2 = 0 in both realizations. No model noise is needed: positive covariance inside the orientation pair defeats the variance identity; in general E[s^2/N] acquires the extra term -2 sum_{i<j} Cov(S_i,S_j) / (N(N-1)).
e2.lindeberg_note: Bounded independent scores do not by themselves give a CLT: for S_t ~ Bernoulli(1/N) independently, all N = 591 scores are 0 with probability (1-1/591)^591 = 0.367568 and the zero-width t interval then excludes the mean 1/591.

task_level.interval_t_status: MODEL-BASED: valid under independent task scores with stable task-specific episode laws and no relevant pass/period effects; NOT implied by the two-pass AB/BA design (the two tasks of a design pair share one orientation coin and complementary pass positions); approximate: additionally needs a Lindeberg / variance-growth regularity condition (boundedness alone is not enough) and a well-behaved variance estimator
task_level.interval_hoeffding_status: exact finite-sample final-time bound ONLY under the same model (independent task scores in [-1,1]); MODEL-BASED: valid under independent task scores with stable task-specific episode laws and no relevant pass/period effects; NOT implied by the two-pass AB/BA design (the two tasks of a design pair share one orientation coin and complementary pass positions)
